title: Building HTTP Servers in Go
intro: Building HTTP servers in Go is straightforward with the standard library, and it is the first thing every Go web developer learns. This module covers http.HandleFunc for registering handlers (the function signature func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)), http.ListenAndServe to start the server, reading the request (r.URL.Query() for query params, r.PathValue() for path params in Go 1.22+, json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&struct) for JSON request body), writing responses (w.Header().Set() for headers, w.WriteHeader() for status codes, json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(&struct) for JSON responses), basic middleware (a function that wraps an http.Handler — the logging middleware pattern), Go 1.22's enhanced ServeMux (method + path routing without a third-party router), and a brief introduction to Gin as the most popular Go web framework and why you might reach for it. Every answer shows the complete, runnable code. The interview question: 'build a simple REST endpoint that accepts a JSON body and returns a JSON response.'
